newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says Italy to use "iron discipline" for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy to use "iron discipline" for EMU.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said in a newspaper interview published on Friday that Italy would use "iron discipline" in order to qualify for the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
In an interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Prodi said that Italy "cannot even allow ourselves to think about delaying (the start) of EMU. We have to run."
Prodi told the newspaper that the most important forces lined up in a campaign against Italy joining EMU are the Bundesbank, German banks and the British press.

"Italy in the past did not fulfill any of the Maastricht criteria," Prodi said. "In contrast to that, we are now filling several of them. For example our inflation rate is 2.5 percent to 2.6 percent. I do not see any difference between Italy and Germany in the fight against inflation."
Now, it was important to use "iron discipline" in order to reduce the budget deficit to below three percent of gross domestic product.
Prodi dismissed the suggestion that Italy was manipulating its accounting in order to qualify, saying every change in book keeping practices are examined in advance by the European institutions.
"Europe is for us a conviction, not just a game," Prodi said.
Prodi said that if Italy failed to qualify for EMU, the country's financial markets could come under a wave of speculative attacks that would lead to devaluation and rising inflation.

"We would become a centre of unrest in Europe," Prodi said.. In a separate interview with the Handelsblatt business daily, Prodi said he was "certain" Italy would be among the first countries to join EMU.
"Italy will belong to the currency union from the start," Prodi said.
